title: Evidence Reference Grammar
description: Canonical machine-readable form of the evidence reference grammar specified in ADR-0004. An evidence reference is an RFC 6901 URI fragment identifier: <source_id>#<json-pointer>. The '#' separator is required. The pointer is either empty (the whole item) or a sequence of '/' prefixed reference tokens, URI-fragment-escaped per RFC 6901 section 3 (~0 decodes to '~', ~1 decodes to '/'; the escape order matters). There is no range syntax: a claim spanning multiple items carries one reference per item.

abnf.const:
evidence-ref    = source-id "#" json-pointer
source-id       = type ":" instance
type            = ALPHA *( ALPHA / DIGIT / "_" / "-" )
instance        = 1*64( UNRESERVED / ":" / "." / "-" / "_" )
json-pointer    = *( "/" reference-token )
reference-token = *( unescaped / escaped )
escaped         = "~" ( "0" / "1" )
unescaped       = %x00-22 / %x24-2E / %x30-7D / %x7F-10FFFF
; array index, RFC 6901 section 4
array-index     = %x30 / ( %x31-39 *(%x30-39) )

const: The '#' separator is required. A reference without '#' is invalid, not a whole-item reference.
The empty pointer (source_id followed by '#') addresses the whole item.
There is no range syntax. A claim spanning multiple items carries one reference per item.
Resolution is a total pure function: (evidence_set, ref) -> value or error. It never raises.
A pointer resolving to an array longer than 20 elements is over_broad_citation: citing a whole collection is not evidence attribution.

'#' is excluded from the unescaped character set because a second '#' would terminate the fragment under RFC 3986; RFC 6901 section 6 requires such a character to be percent-encoded, and a raw reference in this grammar must therefore not contain one.
The escape order matters when decoding: '~1' must be replaced before '~0', so '~01' decodes to '~1' and not to '/1'.

Array indices follow RFC 6901 section 4: the token MUST be '0', or digits without a leading '0' (ABNF array-index = %x30 / ( %x31-39 *(%x30-39) )). '01' and '007' are invalid, and the digits are ASCII only.
Any reference that is present on a claim must resolve, whatever the claim class. Only the requirement to carry a reference is class-scoped.
